title: ～のです — the explaining ending (casual: ～んです)
summary: のです adds an explaining or ‘here is the reason’ feeling to a sentence. It follows the plain form of a verb or adjective, and な-adjectives and nouns take な before の. In conversation it usually becomes んです.

patterns.form: 動詞・い形容詞の普通形＋のです
patterns.gloss: plain form + のです (痛いのです, 行くのです)

patterns.form: 名詞／な形容詞＋なのです
patterns.gloss: noun / na-adjective + なのです (休みなのです)

body.p: A plain sentence only states a fact. Adding のです tells the listener ‘this is the explanation / the situation’. When asking, どうしたのですか means ‘What's the matter?’ and invites an explanation.
Use the plain form before のです: 頭が痛いのです. For a noun or na-adjective, the plain present form is だ, which changes to な before の: 休みなのです, 元気なのです.
In daily speech, のです becomes んです (more polite: んですか). It is softer and more natural than a bare statement when giving a reason or asking about one.

examples.note: Asks for an explanation of the situation.

examples.ja: 頭（あたま）が痛（いた）いのです。
examples.note: Gives the reason or situation. Natural English: ‘My head hurts.’

examples.ja: 今日（きょう）は休（やす）みなのです。
examples.romaji: Kyō wa yasumi na no desu.
examples.tr: It's that today is a day off.
examples.note: Noun 休み takes な before の.

pitfalls: After a noun or na-adjective use なのです, not だのです or のです alone: 休みなのです.
It is not needed in every sentence. Use it when explaining or asking for a reason.
